item.title: Reverse a Short Function to C
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (fastcall: first int arg in ecx; return in eax). Reverse this disassembly to equivalent C:
foo: mov eax, ecx sar eax, 31 xor ecx, eax sub ecx, eax mov eax, ecx ret
What does foo(int x) compute?
---
Answer:
int foo(int x) { return x < 0 ? -x : x; }
Explanation: 1) sar eax, 31 arithmetic-shifts the sign bit across all 32 positions, turning eax into an all-ones mask (0xFFFFFFFF) when x is negative, or all-zeros when x is non-negative. 2) xor ecx, eax is a no-op when the mask is zero, but flips every bit of x (computes ~x) when the mask is all-ones. 3) sub ecx, eax then subtracts the mask: subtracting 0 leaves x unchanged; subtracting -1 is the same as adding 1, so ~x becomes ~x + 1 = -x -- the classic branchless abs() idiom using two's-complement negation.
